physicalNotes: No radius or mass is measured: Gillessen et al. (2017, ApJ 837, 30; VizieR J/ApJ/837/30), table3 gives only its class (early-type) and K = 16.70 mag, and Habibi et al. (2017, ApJ 847, 120) fit spectra of S1, S2, S4, S6, S7, S8, S9 and S12. Radius and GM are recorded as 0: not measured.

sources.period: Derived: Kepler's third law with a = 0.3975 arcsec x 8277 pc = 3290.11 au and the central mass 4.297e6 solar masses (GRAVITY 2022, Table 1): sqrt(3290.11^3 / 4.297e6) = 91.0400 yr of 365.25 d. The table prints no period.
sources.shape: GRAVITY Collaboration (2022, A&A 657, L12), Table 1: a = 0.3975 +/- 0.0016 arcsec, placed at 8277 pc: 3290.1 au, 16324.4 shadow radii; e = 0.9693 +/- 0.0001; i = 144.37 +/- 0.07 degrees. Osculating elements.
sources.phase: GRAVITY Collaboration (2022), Table 1: t_peri = 2021.4104 +/- 0.0002 yr. Decimal year taken as a Julian epoch, MJD = 51544.5 + (year - 2000.0) x 365.25; its time scale is taken as TDB (a difference of about a minute).
sources.orientation: GRAVITY Collaboration (2022), Table 1: Omega = 7.00 +/- 0.33 degrees. This is a Keplerian orbit: no relativistic precession is modelled. Orientation mapped by measurement: Gillessen et al. (2017, ApJ 837, 30; VizieR J/ApJ/837/30) table5 positions and radial velocities of S2 (145 positions, 44 radial velocities, 1992-2016) and S1 (161 positions) are reproduced by this package's hosted orbit with i and Omega as published and omega + 180 degrees (2.08 and 3.17 mas rms, 31.9 km/s rms for S2); every other mapping is off by 135-594 mas or 1551 km/s. The published omega is the star's own argument of periapsis; the hosted-orbit convention stores the host-side one, as the beta-pictoris records do.
sources.argumentOfPeriapsis: GRAVITY Collaboration (2022), Table 1: omega = 205.79 +/- 0.33 degrees, the star's own; stored as 25.79.
